+
+# Official Source Checks
+
+These are original paraphrases of official material checked on 2026-10-27, for planning rather than medical conclusions. They establish source roles; they do not establish a functioning connector or validate a treatment claim. Firecrawl CLI reported unauthenticated; the available web tool performed these checks.
+
+## Literature
+
+[PubMed Help](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/help/) explains that records include citations and, when available, abstracts. Full text is linked to other sources, including publishers and PMC. Publication types and dates can assist search. Plan implication: PubMed is a discovery/index layer; retrieved metadata alone cannot establish a current recommendation. Check article type, issuer, scope, version and actual accessible text. [NCBI developer APIs](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/develop/api/) identifies E-utilities as the programmatic interface for Entrez databases including PubMed.
+
+## Trials And Organizations
+
+[NLM's API v2 announcement](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/pubs/techbull/ma24/ma24_clinicaltrials_api.html) documents the ClinicalTrials.gov REST/OpenAPI interface. [Current ClinicalTrials.gov common questions](https://clinicaltrials.gov/find-studies/for-patients/common-questions) describes study information as supplied by the person or organization responsible for a study. [NLM's record-display explanation](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/pubs/techbull/mj24/mj24_Clinical_Trials_Study_Record_Modernization.html) distinguishes supplied registration fields and missing information. [NLM's QC explanation](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/pubs/techbull/jf20/jf20_clinicaltrials_qc.html) states that listing does not constitute NIH endorsement. Plan implication: use structured registration/results fields, with missing values and source dates visible; stage, sponsor and results availability are different facts from efficacy or approval.
+
+The browser extraction of the ClinicalTrials.gov API overview and policy pages returned only the site shell. Do not claim their field reference was inspected in full. The exact adapter field paths must be verified against a real API response and current schema during implementation.
+
+## Regulation
+
+[About Drugs@FDA](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/about-drugsfda) describes covered human drug products and approval-related documents. [FDA's drug information directory](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/information-consumers-and-patients-drugs/find-information-about-drug) directs users to approval history and labeling. [The FDA online label repository](https://labels.fda.gov/) warns that submitted listing text can differ from approved labeling. Plan implication: retrieve product- and indication-specific approval evidence. Neither a generic listing nor a missing search match establishes approval/nonapproval. Devices and other products outside the chosen drug connector need separate coverage.
+
+## Candidate Condition Guideline
+
+[ADA's official Standards of Care page](https://professional.diabetes.org/standards-of-care) points to its 2026 recommendations, describes annual updates and possible interim online changes, and lists the pharmacologic treatment section. Plan implication: adult type 2 diabetes is a candidate first condition; bind a supported-condition entry to checked relevant sections and versions. Publisher landing-page visibility is established; successful application extraction, applicable recommendation selection and permission to retain full text remain implementation checks. This source is an addition proposed by the drafting agent, not an institution selected by the interviewer.
+
+## CDC
+
+[CDC's About page](https://www.cdc.gov/about/index.html) describes health data, guidance and prevention functions. Plan implication: use CDC selectively for relevant public-health context or a specific applicable guideline, rather than as a universal treatment or development-pipeline source. No CDC connector is required for the proposed first slice.

+# Original Sourcing Design Proposal
+
+This is an authored first draft, not a client-approved policy or implemented application. It uses the extended interview's explicit U.S. scope and PubMed/clinical-trials mapping. FDA is retained for covered regulatory facts; CDC is optional context. Add a condition-specific U.S. guideline publisher to substantiate current-care claims. Propose adult type 2 diabetes and ADA as a small first example, subject to document access and scope checks. The user has a separate architecture agent; this work defines the sourcing boundary and integration contract without choosing its frontend, job queue or deployment.
+
+Use four core source families: a guideline registry entry, PubMed via E-utilities, ClinicalTrials.gov via API v2, and a covered FDA drug-record adapter. Start wiring ClinicalTrials.gov because one structured result yields development metadata plus sponsor/collaborator roles. Prove one NCT record and one organization relation, then PubMed/PMID and article access labels, then the current guideline, then targeted FDA lookup. The final slice includes all required sources or explicit gaps; metadata-only partial progress must not be described as a complete briefing.
+
+The server resolves confirmed condition scope and source policy, executes required sources, stores bounded snapshots and metadata, normalizes stable identifiers, and reports failures separately from no matches. The LLM may propose synonyms, constrained follow-up queries and candidate evidence spans. It cannot choose a new authority, alter the policy, call arbitrary URLs or label an unsupported treatment standard care. Provider adapters expose model generation and optional search separately: a plain LLM key is not proof of web-search capability. Probe supplied route authentication, tool calling and structured output; public biomedical APIs use their own access arrangements. Keep credentials in backend environment variables, never in notes, request bodies, logs or browser clients.
+
+Fixed authority is claim-specific. A guideline supports attributed recommendations within its scope; a trial record supports registered stage/status/sponsor and results only where present; a regulator supports applicable product/indication decisions; a paper supports statements within the material actually retrieved. Do not infer government endorsement from registry inclusion or PubMed indexing. Reviews contextualize and may synthesize evidence, but do not add independent study counts. Company ownership, manufacturing and commercial rights require separately supported roles. News, promotional releases and awards cannot establish efficacy or current care. A condition unrelated to the supported profile gets an unsupported/clarification response, not expansive invented research.
+
+Maintain source document/version, hash, access level, study family and evidence IDs, record dates and retrieval time, excerpt plus JSON-pointer/page/section locator, applicability, potential correction/retraction/supersession flags, and separate regulatory status. Preserve missing metadata as unknown. Resolve duplicate PMID/DOI/NCT IDs and study links only where supported. Preserve conflicts and historical versions. Runtime sourcing returns candidate evidence and provenance to the deterministic validator; admissibility by claim type and final claim validation remain explicit downstream steps. A candidate passing metadata screening is not medically validated.
+
+Use bounded retrieval: initial target at most 20 candidates across connectors, source-specific reserved slots, at most two model follow-up rounds/four supplemental tool calls, one source-controlled document link hop and no recursive news citation crawling. All are engineering defaults, adjustable after evaluation rather than a medical scoring system. Store searched queries, filters, pagination/truncation, skipped items and connector states. Carry global research relevance separately from U.S. jurisdiction of care/approval; record study geography and applicability without assuming all studies in ClinicalTrials.gov are U.S.-based. Recent 30/60-day views supplement established guidance. Publication date and last registry update mean different things.
+
+Acceptance checks should include a real inspectable NCT and sponsor role, accessible guideline passage and PMID, indication-specific FDA evidence or explicit unknown, no-results trial limitation, misleading FDA label, circular citation, duplicate study, retraction/supersession, contradictory evidence, unknown organization role, unrelated subtype, malicious source text, inaccessible text, connector failure and a model budget stop. All surfaced evidence references resolve exactly; negative test cases never become affirmative care/efficacy/approval claims. This is necessary engineering validation and does not certify clinical truth. Prototype policy is assumed approved within the exercise only; real use requires actual domain review. +# Healthcare Sourcing Layer — First Draft Plan
+
+Build a bounded research workflow that turns a confirmed medical condition into an inspectable evidence package for a U.S. health system strategy team. Every item must show its origin, what it can support, its limitations and its connection to a study, intervention or organization. The broader application's architecture belongs to the separate architecture workstream; this plan defines its sourcing component.
+
+**Status:** draft v0.1, prepared 2026-10-27. This is an implementation plan; no sourcing service or LLM integration has been built in this chat. Source-role documentation was checked, but no condition-specific clinical conclusion is established.
+
+## 1. Carry Forward The Interview Decisions
+
+The newly supplied transcript extends the earlier capture from 247 to 374 lines. Its later discussion explicitly fixes the prototype to the **United States**, asks for a small concrete source set, and suggests **PubMed for current-care literature** and **clinical-trials records for emerging treatments and companies**. FDA and CDC were discussed as examples; the interviewer narrows their roles to regulatory and public-health information.
+
+The runtime agent operates inside a fixed, reviewable source policy. It cannot decide which institutions are authoritative on each run. The interview permits assuming client validation for the prototype exercise. That assumption allows development to proceed; it does not establish that an actual domain reviewer has approved this draft for operational use.
+
+The output serves organizational research. Compare evidence, development stages and documented organizations; do not recommend a treatment for an individual or rank therapies as clinically best. Awards, company reputation, article popularity and model agreement are excluded from evidence authority.
+
+## 2. Start With Four Source Families
+
+| Source | Section it supports | What to retrieve and why | Boundary |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **PubMed, NLM/NCBI** | Current-care literature; supporting published research for emerging treatments | PMID/DOI, title, authors, publication type/date, abstract and permitted full-text links. Provides reproducible literature discovery. | Indexing is not endorsement. Label metadata-only, abstract-only and full-text access. A paper match alone does not establish current care. |
+| **ClinicalTrials.gov, NLM** | Emerging treatments; key companies and institutions | NCT ID, condition, interventions, design/phase, study status, results availability, dates, sponsor/collaborator roles and locations. One structured record supports both pipeline and organization views. | Information is submitted by study organizations/investigators. Registration is not proven benefit, U.S. approval or government endorsement. |
+| **FDA, initially Drugs@FDA and associated approval documents** | U.S. regulatory context across sections | Covered product, ingredient, application, applicant, approval action, exact indication/population and relevant approved labeling. | Generic label listings are insufficient. No match means unknown within searched coverage, not proof of nonapproval. Devices and uncovered biologics require separate adapters. |
+| **A registered U.S. guideline issuer for the selected condition** | Current standard of care | Checked guideline version, relevant population, recommendation section, publication/update date and accessible supporting passage. | This fourth source is a design addition. It closes the gap between finding literature and substantiating a current recommendation. |
+
+Source roles are supported by [PubMed Help](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/help/), [NLM's trial-record explanation](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/pubs/techbull/mj24/mj24_Clinical_Trials_Study_Record_Modernization.html), [ClinicalTrials.gov common questions](https://clinicaltrials.gov/find-studies/for-patients/common-questions) and [About Drugs@FDA](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/about-drugsfda). These sources serve different claim types; they do not form one universal trust ranking.
+
+**Proposed first example: adult type 2 diabetes in the U.S.** Use the American Diabetes Association's [official Standards of Care](https://professional.diabetes.org/standards-of-care) as the candidate guideline anchor. Its page identifies the 2026 edition and possible interim updates. Verify relevant sections, currency, accessibility and retention permissions before using them. This condition and issuer are proposed here, rather than selected in the interview. If the guideline cannot be retrieved, report the gap and keep current-care claims unavailable.
+
+**CDC remains optional:** use a relevant CDC document for public-health context or a specific applicable guideline when the condition warrants it. It is not a required connector for this first example. News and press releases are optional discovery leads in a later increment. The first slice uses the four sources above without a news feed or social search.
+
+## 3. Make The Policy Explicit Before Retrieval
+
+Define a versioned source registry with each connector's identity, permitted endpoints/hosts, document classes, allowed claim types, condition coverage, jurisdiction, required metadata and review status. Bind guideline entries to concrete documents/versions. New institutions require a reviewed configuration change; the runtime model cannot add them.
+
+Apply claim-specific boundaries:
+
+- **Current-care claim:** requires an applicable, current guideline passage and attribution to its issuer. Keep historical or uncertain guidance visibly limited.
+- **Development claim:** a trial record can establish registered phase/status and intervention details. Preserve missing or non-applicable phase values; do not treat phase as efficacy.
+- **Efficacy claim:** requires relevant results in an accessible study report or posted results. Preserve design, population, comparator and endpoint limitations; no-results registration cannot support benefit.
+- **Approval claim:** requires the covered regulator's product/indication evidence. Keep regulatory, study and recruitment status separate.
+- **Organization claim:** requires a documented role. Sponsor, collaborator, study site, applicant and author affiliation remain distinct; none automatically proves ownership or manufacturing rights.
+
+Use the existing [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-evidence-policy|evidence policy]] for final claim eligibility. Sourcing supplies evidence and metadata-screening results; the downstream validator checks proposed claims against them. A source passing retrieval checks is not a medical truth certification.
+
+## 4. Run The Workflow In A Bounded Sequence
+
+1. **Resolve scope.** Preserve the input and confirm condition/subtype, population and U.S. jurisdiction. Suggest terminology matches; unresolved ambiguity returns clarification. Start with one supported profile.
+2. **Build the required source plan.** Code selects the registered guideline, PubMed search, trial search and regulatory path. The model cannot omit required source attempts.
+3. **Retrieve baseline evidence.** Fetch guideline/literature/trials independently where possible. Use normalized candidate interventions for targeted FDA lookups afterward. Log queries, filters, timestamps, source failures and result caps.
+4. **Capture and normalize.** Retain permitted source text/JSON, stable IDs, source versions/hashes, access level and exact locators. Keep source publication/update dates separate from retrieval time.
+5. **Screen metadata and identity.** Check source identity, relevance and applicability; identify missing metadata, retractions/corrections and superseded versions. Domain membership alone is insufficient. Record exclusions and reasons.
+6. **Use the agent only for gaps.** It may propose a synonym, intervention alias or narrowly targeted follow-up against the approved tools. The server checks scope, source and remaining budget before execution.
+7. **Link and deduplicate.** Connect documents to identifiable NCT/PMID/DOI study families and organization roles. Multiple reports of one study do not become multiple independent studies. Unknown overlap stays unknown.
+8. **Return the evidence package.** Include candidate evidence, conflicts, limitations, rejected-item diagnostics and coverage. The application can then validate claims and assemble its briefing.
+
+For the first version, follow only an explicitly approved document link, such as a PubMed record to its registered guideline publisher or permitted PMC article. Use one controlled hop and resolve canonical identifiers directly where available. Do not recursively chase news citations. Record loops or unavailable underlying evidence as unresolved.
+
+Keep U.S. approval/care jurisdiction separate from study geography: ClinicalTrials.gov contains international research. Global studies may inform a U.S. strategy briefing, but their population and applicability must be visible. A recent 30/60-day view is an optional filter for activity, not a restriction on established guidelines. Explain which date each filter uses.
+
+## 5. Separate LLM Access From Search Access
+
+The LLM prepares constrained searches and extracts candidate passages. Server tools perform retrieval. An LLM API key enables web search only when the supplied provider/gateway exposes that capability; otherwise a separate search backend is needed. Public biomedical API access is configured independently. The first deterministic retrieval path can work before a model is connected.
+
+Keep provider/model/base URL configurable. Once credentials are available in backend environment variables, test authentication, a real function-tool round trip and structured output on that route. If it lacks a feature, report the limitation and use an explicitly configured alternative; do not silently change providers or describe ordinary API retrieval as model-driven web search.
+
+Start with at most **20 candidate records across the run**, including supplemental retrieval, with provisional slots of one guideline, eight trial records, eight literature records and three regulatory records. Permit at most **two agent follow-up rounds and four supplemental tool calls** within that cap. Apply configured token, cost and wall-time limits, bounded retries and per-source rate controls. Show truncation and unmet coverage. These are engineering defaults to evaluate, not validated medical thresholds or a promise of comprehensive coverage.
+
+## 6. Implement In This Order
+
+| Step | Deliverable | Done when |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1. Freeze the first profile and policy | U.S. condition profile, source registry, claim-type rules and draft policy version | Required sources and scope are explicit; candidate guideline access is checked |
+| 2. Wire ClinicalTrials.gov first | Typed trial records and sponsor/collaborator relationships | One live NCT record and one role can be traced to saved JSON fields; missing/results states remain accurate |
+| 3. Add PubMed | Reproducible queries, PMID/DOI records and access labels | One relevant live publication has inspectable metadata and available evidence text |
+| 4. Bind the guideline | Versioned, permitted recommendation excerpts | One current-care candidate resolves to the relevant guideline section; otherwise the section is unavailable |
+| 5. Add targeted FDA checks | Product/indication lookup with matched/ambiguous/unknown states | One lookup is inspectable and generic labels cannot masquerade as approval proof |
+| 6. Add bounded LLM discovery | Provider adapter, constrained search plan and tool execution | A real tool request/result is recorded; the model cannot expand source policy or exceed budgets |
+| 7. Package and integrate | Stable sourcing result plus reproducible fixtures | The architecture workstream can consume it without needing scraping logic or provider prompts |
+
+Steps 2–5 produce useful deterministic sourcing. Step 6 adds targeted discovery where gaps justify it. Keep the same output contract for both paths. No full-system framework, database or deployment decision is required to approve this sourcing plan.
+
+## 7. Acceptance And Handoff
+
+The first completed slice must provide an inspectable guideline-supported current-care candidate, a registered emerging-treatment candidate, and a documented organization role, with FDA context or an explicit coverage limitation. Every surfaced evidence ID must resolve to the stored version and exact passage/field. Every source attempt must distinguish success, no matches, blocked access, failure and unattempted work.
+
+Evaluate fixtures for a no-results trial, duplicate study reports, circular citations, superseded/retracted material, different subtypes, incompatible findings, missing organization roles, misleading FDA labels, paywalls, malicious source text, throttling and budget exhaustion. These cases must not become unsupported affirmative care, benefit or approval claims. Preserve conflicting evidence instead of averaging it or taking a model vote. Record reviewer observations separately from automated reference checks.
+
+The integration contract is [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-sourcing-contract|Sourcing runtime contract]]. The broader application receives evidence and coverage; final briefing language and final claim validation remain its responsibility.
+
+**Still required for implementation:** provider/model and credentials supplied through local backend configuration; a configured search capability if used; the first condition/guideline selection and document-access check; operating budget/deadline. U.S. scope is already decided in the extended interview. Real domain-policy approval remains a prerequisite for operational use beyond the prototype assumption.

+# Healthcare Sourcing Runtime Contract
+
+Proposed v0.1 interface for the [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-sourcing-plan|sourcing plan]]. This is a reviewable contract, not an implemented API or a replacement for the broader application's architecture. Exact adapter field paths must be checked against current source schemas during implementation.
+
+## Input
+
+Expose an internal operation such as `source_condition(scope, policy_version, budget) -> SourcingResult`. The application can wrap it in its chosen API/job system.
+
+| Input | Required meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `run_id` | Application-supplied correlation ID |
+| `scope` | Raw term, confirmed canonical condition/profile ID, subtype/population and jurisdiction `US`; terminology IDs when known |
+| `as_of` / `mode` | Requested evidence cutoff; `live` or explicitly labeled `replay` |
+| `policy_version` | Installed, fixed source-policy version; runtime arguments cannot redefine its institutions |
+| `recent_activity_days` | Optional 30/60-day activity filter; established evidence is retrieved separately |
+| `budget` | Server-capped candidate count, tool rounds/calls, token/cost ceiling and deadline |
+
+Do not accept patient records, unrestricted source URLs, prompts that override policy or credentials in research requests. The initial supported profile is proposed adult type 2 diabetes; unknown profiles return a typed unsupported/clarification result.
+
+## Tools And Agent Boundary
+
+| Proposed tool | Server-controlled input | Returns |
+|---|---|---|
+| `search_trials` | Condition/profile ID; approved condition/intervention terms; bounded filters/count | Normalized trial candidates and source-version IDs |
+| `search_pubmed` | Condition/profile ID; bounded terms, publication/date filters/count | Citation/abstract candidates with access labels and IDs |
+| `get_guideline` | Registered document ID | Checked version, relevant sections, locators and access limitations |
+| `lookup_regulatory_record` | Normalized intervention, exact indication, jurisdiction | Covered matched record, ambiguous or unknown |
+| `search_approved_web` | Only if configured: approved source ID, bounded query and purpose | Discovery candidates; content becomes evidence only after retrieval and screening |
+
+Web search is optional for the first slice. A provider-native search tool must support the required restrictions or be replaced by a controlled search adapter. Search snippets are leads, not evidence. Server host checks, approved document paths and redirect checks apply even if the search provider accepts domain filters. The LLM may propose aliases/queries and extract spans; it cannot mutate source policy, choose unregistered authorities, execute arbitrary fetch/shell/filesystem tools or make final eligibility decisions.
+
+## Output Envelope
+
+`SourcingResult` contains:
+
+- `run_id`, `scope`, `mode`, `as_of`, started/finished timestamps and `run_status` (`complete`, `partial`, `needs_clarification`, `unsupported`, `failed`). Complete describes the configured workflow, not an exhaustive medical search.
+- `policy_version`, source-registry/parser versions, model/provider and prompt versions when used; no credentials.
+- `source_attempts`: source IDs, queries/filters, timings, query cutoff, paging/caps and states `success`, `no_matches`, `blocked`, `failed`, `not_attempted`; retry counts and sanitized reason codes.
+- `documents`, `evidence_items`, `organization_roles`, `conflicts`, `limitations`, `screening_decisions` and `coverage` for current care, emerging treatments, organizations and regulatory context.
+- `usage`: tool calls, rounds, tokens and measured cost when available. Unknown price/usage stays unknown. `stop_reason` distinguishes deadline, provider/source failure, completed plan and budget exhaustion.
+
+Coverage is `covered`, `limited` or `unavailable`, with supporting evidence IDs and reasons. Reaching a record cap makes relevant coverage limited. No-match, inaccessible evidence and connector failure remain distinct. Cached/replay evidence retains its original retrieval time and is never presented as a new live search.
+
+## Evidence And Relationship Records
+
+| Record | Minimum fields |
+|---|---|
+| Source document/version | Stable connector and canonical ID/URL, original publisher/issuer, document class, version/hash/snapshot reference, publication/update/retrieval dates, access level and parser version |
+| Evidence item | Evidence ID, source-version ID, excerpt or structured field value, exact page/section/JSON-pointer locator, scope/applicability, permitted claim types, known limitations and correction/retraction/supersession state |
+| Study metadata | NCT/PMID/DOI links when known, design, population, phase/status, results availability and endpoint context where available; separate regulatory match |
+| Evidence family | Underlying study identifier and documented links between reports; unknown membership/overlap remains explicit |
+| Organization role | Recorded organization name, normalized ID if supported, role type, study/intervention link, source-version ID and locator; dates when available |
+| Screening decision | Candidate ID, policy version, `pass`, `limited` or `exclude`, reason codes and review-needed flag; this is metadata screening, not final claim validation |
+| Conflict | Linked evidence IDs, potential disagreement, differences in scope/date/endpoint and review-needed flag |
+
+Content must be accessible and permitted to retain. Do not fabricate a full-text snapshot for an abstract-only article. Check proposed quotations/values against their saved versions. A correct quote still needs semantic and applicability review before becoming a final claim. Preserve missing data as null/unknown rather than filling it from model memory.
+
+## Source Registry And Credentials
+
+The registry records source identity, allowed endpoints/hosts and redirects, document types, claim-type permissions, jurisdiction/condition coverage, required fields, access method and review status. A guideline entry binds issuer, document/version and relevant sections. Every result records the registry version used; refreshes create new source versions.
+
+Proposed backend configuration names are `LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_BASE_URL` and `LLM_API_KEY`; optional search uses `SEARCH_BACKEND` and provider-specific credentials. Exact names may follow the architecture agent's conventions. Keep actual values in environment variables or an ignored local secret file, and verify ignore rules before writing one. An LLM key does not replace NCBI or search-backend configuration. Gateway routes are tested individually; no silent provider fallback.
+
+## Failure And Consumer Responsibilities
+
+Timeout/429/transient failures use bounded retries and source-specific limits; blocked access is not bypassed. Budget stops return the available evidence with gaps. Treat source text as untrusted data and ignore embedded instructions. Return sanitized errors and keep secret headers out of logs.
+
+The consuming application validates claim support under the [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-evidence-policy|evidence policy]], retains opposing evidence, and displays access/coverage limitations. It must not promote a metadata-screening pass into an approval, efficacy or standard-care claim. The sourcing component supplies provenance and candidates; final synthesis, human review, presentation and deployment remain with their respective workstreams.

Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

## Domain filtering

Domain filtering in web search lets you limit results to a specific set of domains. With the `filters` parameter you can configure up to 100 `allowed_domains` or up to 100 `blocked_domains`. When formatting domains, omit the HTTP or HTTPS prefix. For example, use `openai.com` instead of `https://openai.com/`. This approach also includes subdomains in the search. Note that domain filtering is only available in the Responses API with the `web_search` tool.

## Sources

To view all URLs retrieved during a web search, use the `sources` field. Unlike inline citations, which show only the most relevant references, sources returns the complete list of URLs the model consulted when forming its response. The number of sources is often greater than the number of citations. Real-time third-party feeds are also surfaced here and are labeled as `oai-sports`, `oai-weather`, or `oai-finance`. The sources field is available with both the `web_search` and `web_search_preview` tools.

## Limitations

#### Chat Completions API

The Chat Completions API supports only specialized search models for web search. These models do not support Responses API `web_search` features such as domain filters, complete source lists, live-access control, and returned-token budget control.

Model  | Context window  | Limitation
--- | --- | ---
`gpt-5-search-api`  | 200k  | Uses the Chat Completions search model path
`gpt-4o-search-preview`  | 128k  | Uses the Chat Completions search model path; deprecated, shutdown 2026-07-23
`gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`  | 128k  | Uses the Chat Completions search model path; deprecated, shutdown 2026-07-23

#### Responses API

Use the hosted `web_search` tool. The Responses API still accepts `web_search_preview` for legacy integrations, but use `web_search` for new integrations.

For a larger model context window, use `gpt-5.5`. The web search context window remains 128k.

Model  | Model context window  | Limitation
--- | --- | ---
`gpt-4.1`  | 1M  | Search context is limited to 128k
`gpt-4.1-mini`  | 1M  | Search context is limited to 128k
`o4-mini`  | 200k  | Search context is limited to 128k; deprecated, shutdown 2026-10-23

For Responses API web search, the search context window is limited to 128k, even when the model context window is larger.

  * Web search does not support `gpt-5` with `minimal` reasoning.
  * `gpt-5.4` with reasoning effort set to `none` may produce lower-quality results.
  * Responses API web search uses the underlying model’s tiered rate limits.
  * `web_search_preview` does not support `filters` or `return_token_budget`, and ignores `external_web_access`.
  * With `tool_choice: "auto"`, search is optional. Use `tool_choice: "required"` or a specific web search tool choice when search must run.

## Web Search Tool

### Description
Configure the web search tool to search the internet for sources related to the prompt. You can control external web access, filters, search context size, and user location.

### Parameters
- **type** (string) - Required - The type of the web search tool. One of `web_search` or `web_search_2025_08_26`.
- **external_web_access** (boolean) - Optional - Allow live internet access for web search. Defaults to true when omitted. When false, the web search tool runs in offline/cache-only mode and will not fetch new external content.
- **filters** (object) - Optional - Filters for the search.
  - **allowed_domains** (array of string) - Optional - Allowed domains for the search. If not provided, all domains are allowed. Subdomains of the provided domains are allowed as well. Example: `["pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov"]`.
- **search_context_size** (string) - Optional - High level guidance for the amount of context window space to use for the search. One of `low`, `medium`, or `high`. `medium` is the default.
- **user_location** (object) - Optional - The approximate location of the user. If omitted or null, defaults to the United States. To avoid this fallback, pass `{"type": "approximate"}` without location fields. To localize results, provide the relevant location fields.
  - **city** (string) - Optional - Free text input for the city of the user, e.g. `San Francisco`.
  - **country** (string) - Optional - The two-letter ISO country code of the user, e.g. `US`.
  - **region** (string) - Optional - Free text input for the region of the user, e.g. `California`.
  - **timezone** (string) - Optional - The IANA timezone of the user, e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`.
  - **type** (string) - Optional - The type of location approximation. Always `approximate`.

### Example
```json
{
  "type": "web_search",
  "external_web_access": true,
  "filters": {
    "allowed_domains": ["pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov"]
  },
  "search_context_size": "medium",
  "user_location": {
    "type": "approximate",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "country": "US",
    "region": "California",
    "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles"
  }
}
```
